title: Thus Saith the First, the Great Command
description: Thus Saith the First, the Great Command in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 116, headed “Love to God and our neighbour, Matt. 22. 37-40”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thus saith the first, the great com-mand, "Let all thy in-ward powers u-nite "To love thy Mak-er and thy God, "With ut-most vi-gour and de-light.

lines: Thus saith the first, the great command,
"To love thy Maker and thy God,
"Then shall thy neighbour next in place
"Measure and rule thy love to him."
This is the sense that Moses spoke,
This did the prophets preach and prove,
For want of this the law is broke,
And the whole law's fulfill'd by love.
But O! how base our passions are!
How cold our charity and zeal!
Lord, fill our souls with heavenly fire,
Or we shall ne'er perform thy will.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
